lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, community associations collected one hundred twenty-four billion dollars.

lines.text: About a quarter went into savings for future repairs. These groups house 78.1 million Americans.
lines.say: About a quarter went into savings for future repairs. These groups house seventy-eight point one million Americans.

lines.text: Back in 1970, it was just 2.1 million people.
lines.say: Back in nineteen seventy, it was just two point one million people.

lines.text: About $93.1B paid running costs like insurance and landscaping; about $31.1B went into reserves.
lines.say: About ninety-three billion paid running costs like insurance and landscaping; about thirty-one billion went into reserves.

lines.text: Reserves are savings for roofs, roads and pools that wear out years from now.
lines.say: Reserves are savings for roofs, roads and pools that wear out years from now.

lines.text: Among homes that pay one, the Census Bureau's median fee was $135 a month in 2024.
lines.say: Among homes that pay one, the Census Bureau's median fee was one hundred thirty-five dollars a month in twenty twenty-four.

lines.text: Picture a hypothetical HOA: 200 homes at that fee is $324,000 a year.
lines.say: Picture a hypothetical HOA: two hundred homes at that fee is three hundred twenty-four thousand dollars a year.

lines.text: Say a roof costs $200,000 more than reserves hold. Split evenly, that's a $1,000 special assessment per home.
lines.say: Say a roof costs two hundred thousand dollars more than reserves hold. Split evenly, that's a one thousand dollar special assessment per home.

lines.text: So an HOA is a tiny government: dues in, bills and reserves out.

post.title: Community associations collected $124.2B in 2025
post.ig:
HOAs, condos and co-ops collected $124.2 billion in dues in 2025, and about one dollar in four went into savings.

373,000 community associations, home to 78.1 million Americans (2025). In 1970: 2.1 million.
$31.1B of 2025 dues went to reserves for roofs, roads and pools; about $93.1B covered running costs.
Median condo/HOA fee: $135 a month in 2024 (Census ACS, 21.6 million homes).
Hypothetical: 200 homes x $135 x 12 = $324,000 a year; a $200,000 reserve gap is $1,000 per home.

Sources: Foundation for Community Association Research 2025 Statistical Review; U.S. Census Bureau 2024 ACS.
News and education, not financial advice.
